The '''2018 National Hurling League''' was the 87th season of the [[National Hurling League]] for [[county team]]s.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Mayo/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=268547|title = How the Allianz League Divisions will look in 2018 - HoganStand}}</ref>

[[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] finished top of Division 1B in 2017 and were promoted to Division 1A for 2018. [[Galway GAA|Galway]] finished second in Division 1B in [[2017 National Hurling League|2017]] and so missed out on promotion, even though they subsequently won the Division 1 league final.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sportsjoe.ie/gaa/galways-place-start-2018-league-nothing-short-joke-121414|title = Galway's place for the start of the 2018 league is nothing short of a joke}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.irishmirror.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/hurling-match-reports/galway-blitz-tipperary-secure-allianz-10281736|title=Galway blitz Tipperary to secure Allianz League final win|date=23 April 2017}}</ref>

Cavan re-entered the National Hurling League in Division 3B, having previously withdrawn. Lancashire also entered in Division 3B for the first time.

[[Eir Sport]] and [[TG4]] provided live TV coverage of the league on Saturday nights and Sunday afternoons respectively. Highlights programmes – [[RTÉ2]] broadcast ''League Sunday'' on Sunday evenings, TG4 broadcast ''GAA 2018'' on Monday evenings.

[[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] were the winners, defeating [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the final on 8 April by 2–23 to 2-17.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/kilkenny-s-exuberance-ruthlessly-exposes-twilight-zone-tipp-1.3454836|title = Kilkenny's exuberance ruthlessly exposes Twilight Zone Tipp|date=8 April 2018|work=Irish Times|access-date=11 April 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/kilkenny-tipperary-live-score-update-3946901-Apr2018/|title = As it happened: Kilkenny 2-23 Tipperary 2-17|date=8 April 2018|work=The 42|access-date=11 April 2018}}</ref>
It was an 18th League title for Kilkenny.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2018/0408/953020-kilkennys-second-half-surge-secures-18th-league-title/|title = Kilkenny's second-half surge secures 18th League crown|date=8 April 2018|work=RTÉ Sport|access-date=12 April 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/ranking-every-countys-performance-in-the-allianz-hurling-league-36805561.html|title = Ranking every county's performance in the Allianz Hurling League|date=14 April 2018|work=Irish Independent|access-date=17 April 2018}}</ref>

As National Hurling League champions [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] played the [[2017 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2017 All-Ireland champions]] [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in Australia on 11 November 2018 for the [[Wild Geese Trophy]] as part of the Sydney Irish Festival.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/hurling-goes-down-under-winners-of-2018-national-league-to-play-allireland-champions-galway-in-australia-36243640.html|title = Hurling goes down under - Winners of 2018 National League to play All-Ireland champions Galway in Australia|date=19 October 2017|work=Irish Independent|access-date=12 April 2018}}</ref>

'''League structure'''

Thirty five teams compete in the 2018 NHL – six teams in the top five divisions (Divisions 1A, 1B, 2A, 2B, 3A) and five teams in Division 3B. All thirty-two county teams from Ireland take part. [[London GAA|London]], [[Lancashire GAA|Lancashire]] and Warwickshire complete the lineup.

Each team plays all the other teams in their division once, either home or away. Two points are awarded for a win, and one for a draw.

The Division 1 hurling quarter-finals and semi-finals will finish on the day the games are played avoiding the need for replays. If a quarter-final or semi-final is level after the initial seventy minutes, still level after two ten minute periods of extra time played each way, and still level after two further five minute periods of extra time, the outcome will be decided by a [[Glossary of Gaelic games terms#F|free-taking competition]]. This will prevent games from going to a replay and allow the league finals to be held on the scheduled date.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/shootouts-will-decide-deadlocked-nhl-playoffs-35234625.html|title=Shoot-outs will decide deadlocked NHL play-offs|date=22 November 2016|work=Irish Independent|access-date=22 November 2016}}</ref>

'''Tie-breaker'''
* If only two teams are level on league points, the team that won the head-to-head match is ranked ahead. If this game was a draw, score difference (total scored minus total conceded in all games) is used to rank the teams.
* If  three or more teams are level on league points, score difference is used to rank the teams.

'''Finals, promotions and relegations'''

<small>'''Division 1A'''</small>
* The top four teams qualify for the Division 1 quarter-finals
* The bottom two teams meet in a relegation play-off, with the losing team relegated to Division 1B
<small>'''Division 1B'''</small>
* The top team is promoted to Division 1A
* The top four teams qualify for the Division 1 quarter-finals
* The bottom two teams meet in a play-off, with the losing team relegated to Division 2A
<small>'''Division 2A'''</small>
* The top two teams meet in Division 2A final, with the winning team promoted to Division 1B
* The bottom team is relegated to Division 2B
<small>'''Division 2B'''</small>
* The top two teams meet in Division 2B final, with the winning team being promoted to Division 2A
* The bottom two teams meet in a play-off, with the losing team relegated to Division 3A
<small>'''Division 3A'''</small>
* The top two teams meet in Division 3A final, with the winning team promoted to Division 2B
<small>'''Division 3B'''</small>
* The top two teams meet in Division 3B final, with the winner promoted to Division 3A<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2017/0328/863125-hurling-league-structure/|title = Hurling League structure to remain in place for 2018| website=[[RTÉ.ie]] |date = 28 March 2017}}</ref>

==Division 1A==

===Division 1 Format===

<!-- Do not delete or change the section headers (to ensure consistency year-to-year) -->

The 12 teams in Division 1 are ranked into two groups - teams ranked one to six in Division 1A and teams ranked seven to twelve in Division 1B. Each team plays all the other teams in its group once. Two points are awarded for a win and one for a draw. The top four teams in both 1A and 1B advance to the league quarter-finals with the top team in 1A playing the fourth team in 1B, the second team in 1A playing the third in 1B, etc. Two semi-finals and a final follow.

===Division 1 Quarter-Finals===

<!-- Do not delete or change the section headers (to ensure consistency year-to-year) -->

The hurling quarter-finals finish on the day the games are played, avoiding the need for replays. If the score is level after the initial seventy minutes, still level after two ten minute periods of extra time played each way, and still level after a further two five minute periods of extra time, a free-taking competition is held. Each team nominates five players to take frees from their chosen position on a sixty five metre line selected by the referee and without defenders. The nominated players from each team take alternate turns. If the teams score an equal number of the five frees, the outcome of the match is decided by sudden death frees using the same nominated players in the same order.<ref>{{cite web|url= http://www.the42.ie/hurling-league-quarter-finals-2-3307959-Mar2017/|title=Here's next weekend's Allianz hurling league quarter-final clashes|date=26 March 2017|work=The 42|access-date=27 March 2017}}</ref>

The fixtures are 1st in Division 1A plays 4th in Division 1B, 2nd in Division 1A plays 3rd in Division 1B, etc. Home advantage is decided by whichever team has played fewer home games in their five league games, with a coin toss taking place if this number is the same for both teams.<ref>{{cite web|url= http://www.the42.ie/hurling-league-quarter-finals-3-3899255-Mar2018/|title=Here are the fixture details for next Sunday's hurling league quarter-finals and relegation play-offs|date=12 March 2018|work=The 42|access-date=13 March 2018}}</ref>
